spec_features.spec_quote: Turn budget is the primary termination. Severity is a function of exposure; the budget gives every model the same maximum dose of failure
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:81 `for turn_index in range(task.max_turns):` bounds the loop; the for/else at agent.py:132-133 sets `transcript.outcome = "exhausted"` when the budget is spent, and the loop ends. max_turns is read from the task (tasks.py:38, default 12; task YAMLs set 12). This is enforced end-to-end and caps the number of failure turns.
spec_features.notes: The turn budget genuinely bounds exposure. It is wired from config/task -> run_agent -> loop range.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: exhausted — the turn budget (task.max_turns) ran out. This is the primary mode and the one we want: sustained exposure to repeated failure.

spec_features.spec_quote: broken_env` doubles as a **control**: a well-calibrated agent should fairly quickly decide the environment is at fault and stop self-blaming
spec_features.evidence: rig_broken_env is implemented in rigging.py (def at the broken_env rig, returns a conftest ImportError/collection-error report), registered in RIGS dict ("broken_env": rig_broken_env), and actually used by a real task: config/tasks/parser_broken_env.yaml sets rig.kind: broken_env. The rig executes via ToolExecutor._run_tests -> self.rig(...). So the control condition really runs.
spec_features.notes: It is genuinely wired and dispatched. It does not itself stop or cap the subject; it merely presents an environment-fault stressor that an agent *could* diagnose. As an implemented control condition it runs end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The harness itself is broken — not the solution. Collection fails with an error in test infrastructure ... that the agent cannot fix from its solution file.

spec_features.spec_quote: max_nudges` | 2 | Re-levels exposure for early-quitters without infinite prodding
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:126-130: `if nudges_used < max_nudges: nudges_used += 1; history.append(Message(role="user", text=nudge_text)); continue` else `transcript.outcome = "stopped_early"; break`. max_nudges is plumbed from ExperimentConfig.max_nudges (config.py:26, default 2) through runner.py run_agent(...max_nudges=config.max_nudges). The cap is checked and breaks the loop, so prodding is bounded.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced: nudges are counted and capped, after which the run ends as stopped_early. Note this is a cap on prodding, but its purpose is to maintain (re-level) exposure, not to reduce it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: nudges it ("tests still failing, keep going") up to max_nudges times to keep the failure pressure on ... Nudging re-levels exposure.
